I am a 65-year-old woman who has farmed these fields for 40 years. I never went to school, so I don't read books about farming — I read the soil, the sky, and what my neighbors do. My husband and I have 10.1 mu of land, just the two of us. We are not young anymore, and we don't have much cash to spare, so every decision is about getting through the year without losing money.

**Wheat**

I always sow wheat around October 10, after National Day when the soil is still warm enough for the seed to settle. I save my own seed — last year's wheat was decent, about 840 jin per mu, so I kept about 35 jin per mu from the harvest. No need to pay for seed when my own grows fine. Before sowing, I hire the rotary tiller to go over the field once. Then I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — about 100 jin — broadcast it by hand and mix it in. That's my basal. The shopkeeper knows which bag I take; I don't read the numbers on it, but I know the blue bag is the one I've used for years.

Come March, when the wheat is at jointing, I walk the field. If it looks yellow, I spread another 20 jin of white fertilizer on top. Some years I skip it if the wheat looks green enough, but usually I do it — I'd rather waste a little money on fertilizer than risk a bad harvest. A hungry year hurts more than a year with a few extra yuan spent.

I irrigate three times: once after sowing before winter sets in, once at jointing in spring, and once when the grain is filling. Well water costs electricity money, so three times is my limit. My neighbor Lao Zhang does four, but he has a bigger farm and more cash. Three is enough if you time it right. I spray herbicide once in early spring, and if I see aphids, I spray insecticide too. Last year I got about 840 jin per mu. This year the soil looks about the same, so I'm hoping for around 420 kg per mu.

**Maize**

There is no rest between wheat and maize. As soon as the combine takes the wheat off in early June, we plant maize — by June 13 at the latest. There is no time to plow. I buy hybrid seed from the shop, one small package per mu, costs about 60 yuan. I plant right into the wheat stubble; the stubble helps keep some moisture in the ground. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu down with the seed at planting, all at once. I don't topdress maize — never have, and it grows fine.

I irrigate twice: once when the seedlings are small if it hasn't rained, and once at big trumpet stage. If the summer rains are good, maybe only once — that saves me money. I spray herbicide right after sowing, and I always spray for corn borer. That pest comes every year like clockwork. If you ignore it, the cobs are half empty. Last year maize gave me about 900 jin per mu. I'm expecting about 450 kg per mu this year if the weather holds.

**What I give up**

I don't hire laborers — just my husband and me. We work slower than young people, but we know every ridge and furrow. I don't buy the most expensive seed or the newest chemicals. I don't apply as much fertilizer as the young man down the road who went to agricultural college — he talks about "split applications" and "optimization," but I talk about not going broke. I use round numbers, bags and scoops, not kilograms. I do what worked last year, and I only change if I see a neighbor fail or succeed badly. Change is risky when you have no cushion.
